title: platform_audit_log is paged without a tie-break (ORDER BY created_at DESC only): windowed reads can repeat or skip rows that share a timestamp
description:
## BLUF

`GET /api/audit-log` in tenant-provisioning pages `platform_audit_log` with `ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT $1 OFFSET $2` and **no tie-break column**. Two rows with the same `created_at` have no defined relative order, and Postgres does not promise the same order across two separate queries. That was harmless while the gateway read the platform half in ONE request; once the gateway reads it in sequential windows (PR for KS-1512), a group of rows sharing a timestamp that straddles a window boundary can be **duplicated or skipped** on a deep page. Reasoned from the SQL and the schema; **not measured, and not seen in any data**.

## Recommendation

P4, one line in `services/tenant-provisioning/src/index.ts`: `ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC` (the table has `id UUID PRIMARY KEY` in both definitions). The existing index `idx_platform_audit_time` is on `created_at DESC` only, so check the plan before and after on a table of realistic size. Test first: a stub or a real table with more than 200 rows sharing one `created_at`, read in two windows, asserting no id appears twice and none is missing. It changes another service than the gateway, which is why KS-1512 did not do it.

## Detail

* **Where:** `Blockchain/Dev/services/tenant-provisioning/src/index.ts:558` (at develop `425ad3e00ae4`): `SELECT * FROM platform_audit_log ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT $1 OFFSET $2`. Schema: `Blockchain/Dev/docker/init-platform/01-platform-schema.sql:119-129` and `Blockchain/Dev/migrations/003_platform_tenancy.sql:49-59`, both with `id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()` and `created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now()`.
* **Why a tie is plausible, not just theoretical:** `now()` is the transaction start time, so several rows inserted in one transaction share the same `created_at` to the microsecond. Whether any code path writes several `platform_audit_log` rows in one transaction I have **not checked** (the four inserts at `index.ts:283, 415, 469, 537` are separate statements; their transaction boundaries were not read).
* **A second, unrelated effect of windowed reads:** a row inserted between two windows shifts the later window by one, so one row can repeat. The old single request had neither effect. Both are rare and bounded to the deep pages (limit + offset above 200).
* **Related:** KS-1512 (the windowed read), KS-1359 (the route's bounds).
* **Dedupe before filing:** literal, case-insensitive matches over titles AND descriptions in team KS, archived included: `tie-break` 0, `ORDER BY created_at` 1 (KS-1072, the latest-anchor selector, a different table and defect), `platform_audit_log` 1 (KS-1512 itself, whose description has no `tie`, `order by` or `duplicate`: 0, 0, 0; the same grep finds `overfetch` and `clamp` in it, so it can read that text). The same instrument returns KS-1512 for a phrase from its own title, so it can see ticket text.

## MERGED — and two residues, one of which corrects the note I was handed

**[#1600](https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/1600) merged as `4f92eef4a32b813d220ef7f5f0735fcda25cc619`** on gate O2's GO (Sonnet, tier 2, 2026-10-19T00:55:27Z). `GET /api/audit-log` in tenant-provisioning now pages `platform_audit_log` with `ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC`. Five-point check 5/5; the landed tree is the tree I tested (`9bdd15e27bc783c25554fa00bedae0e6273cfc9f`), and I re-measured `services/tenant-provisioning` there at **21/21 in 5 files** rather than carrying the author's figure, because the PR's evidence said "delta 0, the landing tree" and that had stopped being true — develop had moved seven commits.

**This ticket stays open**, and the link is `Refs`, because the PR pins the ORDER BY *text*, not the paging *behaviour* this ticket's own test spec asks for (>200 rows sharing one `created_at`, read in two windows, no id duplicated or missing). The query-plan check is also still owed.

## Residue 1 — the same missing tie-break on the gateway's `audit_logs` reads, but a *different* consequence

I was asked to record that "the same tie-break gap exists on the gateway's `audit_logs` query". It does — and the consequence is **milder than a paging hazard**, which is worth stating so nobody sizes it wrongly:

| site | query | paged? |
|---|---|---|
| `services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts:447-453` | `SELECT … FROM audit_logs ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT $1` (`overfetch`) | **no OFFSET** |
| `services/api-gateway/src/routes/admin.ts:1542` | `SELECT * FROM audit_logs ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1000` (CSV export) | **no OFFSET** |

Neither uses OFFSET, so there is **no window boundary** and therefore none of the duplicate-or-skip behaviour this ticket is about. What they do have is a nondeterministic **cut**: among rows tied on `created_at`, *which* ones fall inside the `LIMIT` is not promised to be stable between two calls. For the CSV export that means two exports a second apart can differ by a tied row; for `platform.ts` the overfetch is then merged with the platform half and sliced in JS, so the same instability reaches the page the UI renders. Both want `, id DESC` for the same reason — just not for the same failure.

## Residue 2 — the index note I was handed is wrong for one provisioning path and right for the other, and the divergence is the real finding

The note said "there is no index on `platform_audit_log`". Measured:

| path | indexes on `platform_audit_log` |
|---|---|
| **migrations** (`migrations/003_platform_tenancy.sql:49` creates the table) | **ZERO** — no `CREATE INDEX` naming that table anywhere under `migrations/` |
| **docker-init** (`docker/init-platform/01-platform-schema.sql`) | **three** — `idx_platform_audit_actor (actor_id)` `:131`, `idx_platform_audit_action (action)` `:132`, `idx_platform_audit_time (created_at DESC)` `:133` |

Counts: 0 hits under `migrations/`, 3 under `docker/` — so the zero is a real absence, not a failed search.

**So a migrations-provisioned database — which is the deployed path — has no index on this table at all, while a docker-init local stack has three.** That is a schema divergence between the two provisioning paths, and it is the kind that hides: a developer profiling this query locally gets an index-backed plan that production does not have. It also means the ticket's own framing ("`idx_platform_audit_time` is on `created_at` alone") describes the *local* schema, not the deployed one.

Two things follow, and I have not done either:
1. The deployed schema should be read directly to confirm the absence on the live boxes (the DDL is the prediction, not the measurement).
2. Whichever index is added should be `(created_at DESC, id DESC)`, to cover the ordering this PR just introduced rather than only its first column.

---

*Seat R 51st, 2026-10-19. Residue 1 and 2 were handed to me as notes from gate O2; I read the source and the schema before writing them here, which is why both are stated differently from how I received them. Measured at develop `37834600a543cb0276f427d969ac034d9df74fbd`. Nothing deployed.*
